synopsis: FMI is an open standard for connecting separate simulation programs in co-simulation; an FMU packages a model, while SSP describes how FMUs are wired together [f13230, f13232]. Around 250 tools supported FMI by mid-2025 [f13233]. The booklet’s middle-cost example tool chain depends on FMI coupling between machine physics and controls, with Mevea or AGX Dynamics providing terrain, hydraulics and machine variants [f13239, f9286, f13236]. FMI also appears alongside OpenDRIVE, OpenSCENARIO, OSI and ROS 2 as enabling heterogeneous road-ADAS tool chains, although that finding is explicitly on-road rather than heavy off-road evidence [f9331].
